_freeze.note: Row 3 authored this file. `frozen` blocks are frozen against ONE thing: moving a number so that an image which failed passes. They are not frozen against extension to an object class no constructed control covered (see `classes` and `amendment`), and they are not frozen against Kabe.

gates.amendable_by: the Navigator, via `classes`, with a constructed control of that class landing in the same commit

camera.amendable_by: row 4, after the probe — blueprint §5: the camera is whatever the room Kabe loves turns out to have

_freeze.amendment: A threshold may never move because a real arriving image failed. That fork is the Navigator's, and its two outcomes are: the image is regenerated, or the row's target moves — and if a target moves, the closing report states which image failed which gate at what measured value.

camera.focal_mm_note: 50 -> 24 at row 20, on blueprint 10's lens ruling [HUMAN, 2026-08-21, "full steam ahead"]: interiors render at a pinned LENS, f = 1024 px on the 1536-wide frame, which is exactly 24 mm on the 36x24 format this frame is. src/groundplane.js holds the pixel constant and tools/plan-projection.mjs's assertRuledLens pins it to THIS field, so the two cannot drift; the bake refuses when they do.

prompt_block: Front-three-quarter view turned 30 degrees to viewer-left, shot at 24 mm, camera at 1.83m eye height pitched approximately 8 degrees downward, object centered and fully in frame with a generous even margin on every side, single soft key light from upper left at 45 degrees with even fill, plain mid-grey seamless background, sharp focus edge to edge, all moving parts closed and fully seated, panel and drawer edges clearly delineated with visible reveal gaps, nothing resting on or in front of the object, no props, no scene
negative_block: cast shadow on background, dramatic lighting, rim light, vignette, depth of field, cropped, background scenery, props
style_block: AUTHORED AT ROW 4 PROBE — extracted from the Kabe-approved study/N backdrop and written here before any sprite generation: palette (named hexes), medium (e.g. painterly gouache vs photoreal), grain/texture character, period rendering descriptors. Every backdrop AND sprite prompt appends it; the sprite hand reads this file and nothing else for style.
backdrop_block: Interior view at 1.183m eye height, camera perfectly level with zero tilt, 1536x1024, one dominant key light per frame whose screen direction and colour are this facing's own and are recorded in its meta as key_dir and key_tint, no rim light, no vignette, no sun shafts across the floor, floor running to the bottom edge of frame, no furniture, no props, door frame or opening only where the section 11 wall map places one.

_backdrop_block_status.status: provisional — authored by row 3 [AI], awaiting Kabe, and it must not become effective by silence
_backdrop_block_status.why_not_section_10_verbatim: §10's placeholder text reads 'overcast diffuse daylight through any window, no visible sun shafts'. §11 marks that phrasing superseded 2026-08-20 by Kabe's look reference — warm practicals against a cool window — and says the real light design lands in Kabe's probe loop. Writing the superseded phrase into the file every backdrop prompt appends would hard-code a look Kabe has already ruled against. So this block states the constraint that matters (one dominant key per frame, recorded per facing) and leaves the direction to the probe.
_backdrop_block_status.eye_height_and_pitch: 1.83m and -8 degrees, not §10's prose 1.6m: the intention's quality 5 names 6 ft per Kabe's 2026-08-20 ruling and `camera.eye_height_m` already carried it. Pitch appears here because a sprite generated level and composited into a room shot at -8 degrees will not foreshorten its top surface like the floor it stands on. NOTE for the Navigator: blueprint §5's horizon device and §12.5's assertion still read 1.6m, which cannot both be right while quality 5 rides on the answer.
_backdrop_block_status.closed_fork_key_dir_per_facing: CLOSED 2026-08-22, at row 21, under blueprint §10's own recorded disposition and the Navigator's ruling relayed the same day. The fork was: "If key_dir varies per facing, ONE sprite set cannot match every room ... It must be answered before row 4's prompt sheets are written." Its antecedent is now a measured fact rather than a hypothetical: the one approved, promoted backdrop — backdrops/study/N.png, blessed by Kabe on 2026-08-21 — measures its key at L-BELOW, the hearth fire, left of centre and below the horizon, against this contract's UL45. THE RULE: a facing whose MEASURED key defies UL rules its own staged sprites' light, as one more dimension of the variant manifest; UL45 remains the default for a facing that is unmeasured or whose measured key is neutral. So study/N's sprite set generates fire-lit, L-BELOW. This costs a light variant per defying facing and it buys the intention's first quality, one light, which the probe composite already proved cannot be had any other way. Row 4's prompt sheets read the promoted meta's key_dir, not this block's default.

alpha_opaque.basis: The threshold for every derivation that asks whether a pixel is OPAQUE, named exactly and no wider: `anchors.base.y`, the footprint's contact columns, and the carcass-backing measure the slide gate's floor is computed from. 128 is the value the shipped tests/playwright/mechanisms.spec.mjs already applies to the same questions, so an ingested record and the shipped witness agree by construction. Row 3 is the first row whose images have a genuinely soft edge, so >0 and >=128 differ by real pixels — `test_clause_guards.py` proves the value is live by moving it and watching base.y and the footprint move. An earlier basis also claimed gate (c)'s content bbox and the thumb's: neither reads it (gate (c) measures the matted SOURCE's height before any alpha exists to threshold, and the thumb's bbox is alpha > 0 because a thumb must not crop its own feather). The claim was removed rather than the code bent to it.
alpha_opaque.solid_basis: `solid_value` is the separate, stricter threshold for derivations that ask whether a pixel is FULLY covered rather than merely present: gate (e)'s third-tilt sample and the record's chroma mean. Both average colour, and a half-covered rim pixel carries the ground's colour in proportion to its own transparency, so sampling it would pull the mean toward the studio grey. It was a bare module constant until row 3's recheck found the light block's basis citing a number the contract did not carry.

halo.min_edge_softness_ratio_basis: a4's fallback, and the answer to a real hole: when the composited rim could not be measured over ANY ground the gate returned green, and a hard-edged silhouette -- the sticker tell itself -- is exactly what leaves no rim at draw scale. It cannot simply hard-fail on absence either, because an axis-aligned silhouette survives a bilinear downscale with no partial coverage while being perfectly feathered natively (the constructed clean control is such a rectangle). So the question moves to where it can be answered: the stored sprite's own boundary. The matte's feather is ONE PIXEL wide by construction, so a real matte has at least one partial-alpha pixel per boundary pixel. Measured: clean 1.01, legged 1.20, neutral disc 1.92, squat disc 1.00 -- and the same sprite with its alpha thresholded to 0/255 scores exactly 0.00. 0.5 sits in the middle of a gap with nothing in it, and it follows from the feather width rather than from any corpus.
halo.min_deep_saturation_basis: a2 is a RATIO of the inner band's saturation to the deep interior's, and a ratio is undefined when its denominator is zero. On a genuinely achromatic object — R=G=B, which is what a neutrally rendered iron key or silver coin is — the deep interior's saturation is exactly 0, the denominator clamps to 1e-9, and the ratio evaluates to 0: gate (a) HARD-FAILS the object for having no colour, and no regeneration can fix it. That is precisely the false-fail the whole ratio form was adopted to prevent, reappearing at the limit. Below this floor a2 is declared UNMEASURED and reported by name, and a3 — the ground-distance ratio, which is the clause written to carry signal when the object has no saturation at all — carries the verdict alone. 0.02 sits below the constructed iron disc (86,88,92 -> 0.065) and above the achromatic control's 0.000; `synth.neutral_disc` is that control, added because the control set had no true R=G=B member and so could not have found this.
halo.basis: a2/a3 are ratios of a depth-2..4px band to the deep interior, so a uniformly grey object (an iron key, a silver coin) is not punished for being grey. Constructed controls: clean 0.988/0.918, legged 0.998/1.094, iron disc 1.000/1.000, grey-halo control 0.047/0.305 — 0.55 sits between them. a4 is the CONTRACT authority and needs no fitted number at all: straight-alpha compositing says a rim pixel of coverage a over ground G against local interior L must land at a*L + (1-a)*G, so the normalized residual is zero for a correct edge whatever the colours are. Constructed clean cases give |median| 0.019-0.155; the grey-halo control gives 0.305 dark / 0.519 light. Known sensitivity limit, stated rather than hidden: a ~2px generator antialias band scores about 0.10 and passes — which is why the MATTE erodes it rather than the gate catching it.
halo.an absolute edge-distance clause was dro: An earlier draft required the semi-alpha ring's mean distance from the ground to exceed a fixed number. That cannot work: an iron key's own colour is about that far from mid-grey, so the clause would false-fail the object rather than the halo. Its relative form is a3.

holes.basis: Gate (b) re-hunts at 2.2x the matte's own computed tolerance, so a gap whose interior is a graded grey the matte's net missed is still caught; at one tolerance the gate could not fail by construction. Its minimum area is the matte's own rule, so a region the matte deliberately declined to punch is also beneath the gate's notice. The flood is seeded from the border AND every transparent pixel, so the wider-tolerance fringe around an already-punched hole is reached and not counted — without that seeding every real image fails.

state_diff.reference: the matted RGBA BEFORE the cavity inpaint
state_diff.basis: The reference is named because two readings differ: against the SOURCE image the matte's own erosion, feather, decontamination and bleed differ along the entire silhouette by construction, so the gate would need an unspecified excluded band. Against the pre-inpaint matte it measures exactly the cut and the inpaint. WHAT IT THEREFORE CANNOT SEE: a matte defect — that is gate (a) and gate (g)'s job, and this gate is not evidence about the matte. Zero pixels over is unachievable on a pipeline that feathers and blurs; 64 pixels over a channel diff of 8 is four orders of magnitude below a leaked inpaint, which moves tens of thousands.

light.basis: expected_deg is the ESTIMATOR'S OWN measured response to a constructed correctly-UL45-lit solid, not the geometric 135 degrees: a Sobel bright-side estimate has a systematic pull toward 90 for any top-lit object, and using 135 forces a band so wide it admits everything from overhead to horizontal-left. Constructed controls: UL 115.3, TOP 90.0, UR 64.7 — a 15-degree band admits UL and rejects both others by 10.2 and 35.6 degrees. min_third_tilt 2.0 is exactly the shipped mechanisms.spec clause ('every sprite carries the horizontal half of UL45'), so a pass here predicts that Playwright case instead of disagreeing with it: UL +35.1, UR -35.1, TOP 0.0.
light.severity: WARN ONLY, per blueprint §9.4(e) [HUMAN]. See the closing report: both corpus desks warn, so no automated check of the intention's 'one light' quality survives row 3 on real art. That is a fork for the Navigator, not a threshold to move.

contact.basis: The footprint is DERIVED from the contact band — the x-extent of columns whose lowest opaque pixel lies within band_fraction of the content height of the bottom. An absolute-fraction floor was rejected: it would hard-fail every three-quarter sprite unless a human measured it first, which makes the autonomous sprite lane the intention promises impossible. band_fraction 0.25 is set on a constructed legged object whose stance is known by construction (true span 20..640 of 658; the derivation returns 20..638 at 0.25 and only the near pair at 0.20) and checked against a constructed squat disc, where it stays proportionate. disagreement_warn_ratio 3.0 passes the legged control (1.29) and the disc (2.82) and warns where a real judgement was made.

over_matte.basis: max_erode_excess_ratio compares the erosion's ACTUAL area loss against what the silhouette's own perimeter predicts, so it is size-independent: a flat area budget rejected a small disc for being small rather than thin. Constructed controls all measure 1.00-1.30; the ratio only climbs when erosion eats a feature thinner than itself, and a vanished connected component is a separate hard failure. Tolerance sensitivity is |A(0.75t) - A(1.25t)| / A(t) on this image's own computed tolerance. Constructed: clean 0.0000, legged 0.0000, iron disc 0.0000, part source 0.0000, and a control with a pale limb six levels off the ground 0.0340. A fixed conservative tolerance was tried first and rejected — at tolerance 5 the ground's own noise stopped the flood fill and the conservative silhouette swallowed the frame, failing a good image for a reason unrelated to the object.

shadow.basis: A shadow lies BELOW the thing that casts it, and that — not tone — is what separates it from a legitimately grey object. The measure is the share of opaque pixels that are ground-toned AND sit below the lowest non-ground-toned opaque pixel in their own column, so a uniformly grey object scores zero by construction. Constructed: clean 0.0000, legged 0.0000, iron disc 0.0000 (it is 98.9% ground-TONED and still scores zero here, which is the point — an earlier tone-fraction draft would have hard-failed the key, the coin and the candlestick by material), shadow control 0.0595.

part_mask.basis: Per-edge, and the score is the WORST edge, not a mean over the whole ring: a mask correct on three sides and 30px out on the fourth averages to a pass, and gate (d) at closed cannot see it either because the over-cut pixels are covered by the part at closed. Set on the constructed part control in synth.py, whose reveal gaps are known by construction: the exact mask scores 1.00, and masks displaced 20px in, 20px out, or 30px on a single edge all score 0.00. Warn-level rather than hard because real generated art is far noisier than the control — a drawer's own highlight band is nearly as dark as its reveal, and the corpus desk's fitted mask scores 0.21 on its worst edge while visibly following the reveals in the overlay. That gap between control and corpus is exactly why this warns and does not block, and the evidence a mask follows the edges is the overlay image `replicator.maskgen --overlay` writes for the eye.

registration.basis: The alignment gate's clause (i) has exactly one satisfying origin.y, so an operator who never opens the images and simply subtracts passes it every time — it certifies nothing. This clause compares the typed --state-origin against an origin DERIVED from the two source images by normalized cross-correlation of a datum patch, in BOTH axes, which is where x registration stops being unverifiable.
registration.min_datum_contrast_basis: Normalized cross-correlation divides out contrast, so a patch of near-uniform studio grey with a level of dither correlates at 1.000 against ANY other patch of the same grey — the recheck found `--state-datum` naming a blank corner scoring a perfect peak at a wrong origin, reported green. The only guard was a zero-variance refusal at 1e-6, which no real image ever trips. min_datum_contrast is the patch's luminance standard deviation in 0..255 units: 3.0 is above the studio ground's own measured noise on both corpus sources (sigma 0.9 and 1.2) and far below any patch containing an actual edge (the corpus desk's drawer jamb measures 41). A datum below it is refused BY NAME rather than silently trusted.
registration.min_peak_margin_basis: Contrast alone does not make a patch unique — a repeated moulding correlates equally well at several offsets and the argmax among them is arbitrary. min_peak_margin is how far the winning peak must stand above the best peak outside a one-patch-radius exclusion zone. 0.05 passes the corpus jamb (margin 0.31) and refuses a synthetic repeated-stripe control.
registration.search_fraction_basis: How far the datum is hunted, as a fraction of the source's longest side. It was a bare `max(shape) // 4` inside locate_datum, and it is load-bearing in a way nothing admitted: a true displacement outside the window cannot be found, and the argmax then lands on whatever the window's edge happened to contain. The gate now also refuses a peak sitting ON the boundary — a winner there is evidence the window was too small, not evidence the feature was found, because the correlation surface is still climbing when it runs out of room. 0.25 covers a door leaf swinging through its own width; widen it per class rather than trusting an edge peak.
registration.no_datum_is_hard: Absent a datum this gate measures NOTHING, and a swap sprite's whole geometry rests on it. It was warn-only, so a swap sprite with a typed, unverified origin exited 0 with an [ok]-adjacent line. It is now HARD: a swap sprite either carries a datum the images can be correlated on, or it does not ship.

alignment.basis: The closed-frame alignment tolerance, as a fraction of body height: how far `origin.y + state height` may sit from the body's bottom edge before the two state images are standing on different floors. It was a bare `0.02 * bh` inside states.py — a HARD gate with no authority, no basis and no entry in the freeze, so `provenance.contract.thresholds_sha256` did not move when it changed and the record's claim to be traceable to the threshold set that admitted it was false. 2% of body height is one pixel of the 89 px draw height at the corpus desk's 384 px stored height, which is the resolution at which a floating leaf is visible.

thumb.basis: Both clauses are HARD and both were bare literals inside thumbs.py, outside the freeze and outside the identity hash. min_coverage 0.01 is the share of the tile that must carry any alpha at all: below it the inventory strip shows an empty square, and 1% of a 128px tile is a 13px mark — smaller than anything a person would call an object. edge_margin_px 2 is how close the content bbox may come to the tile's own edge before it has been clipped rather than fitted: the fit targets content_px 112 inside size_px 128, so a bbox reaching within 2px of 128 means the fit did not happen.

dims.basis: The band inside which the declared footprint and the drawn pixels are the same object. It was a bare `0.85 <= ratio <= 1.15` inside record.py, so the one gate that catches comparison-criteria's own T5.3 (scale disagreement) was not in the threshold set the record claims to be traceable to. +/-15% is the slack the unsettled §5 camera and a period reference measurement together deserve; beyond it the record and its own pixels are describing different furniture. Warn and not hard because `dims_m` is the operator's and §5's camera is genuinely unsettled — but the row-3 corpus desk shipped at ratio 0.70 with this warn firing, which is why the closing pass re-declared its width from its own pixels instead.

tolerance_rule.basis: The contract asserts a 'perfectly plain seamless uniform mid-grey background', so the ground's own noise is measurable on the border of every arriving image and the tolerance is COMPUTED per image rather than fitted to any corpus. k_sigma 8 is eight standard deviations of that measured noise — the separation at which a pixel is not the ground; drift_multiplier covers the residual non-uniformity a single border median cannot represent, measured as the spread of the four corner medians on the same image, which is why no constant is needed for it. The min/max clamps bound the rule where an image's border is pathologically clean or pathologically noisy: below 8 a lossy encoder's own ringing is treated as object, above 32 an oak brown starts to fall inside the net.

spatial_rule.basis: Every spatial parameter scales with the content bbox rather than being an absolute pixel count, because the contract admits sources from 128px of content (a takeable at gate (c)'s floor) to well over 1000 (the corpus): 2px of erosion is 0.2% of one and 1.6% of the other, and a 64px minimum hole area is 4% of the whole of the smaller. hole_side_fraction 0.010 says a gap a person drew is at least 1% of the object's height on a side. erode_fraction gives 2px at 900px of content and 1px at 128 — the depth measured, and looked at, as the one that removes the generator's own antialias band against the studio grey.
spatial_rule.why_erode_at_all: The generator antialiases the object against the mid-grey seamless, so the outermost 1-3px of the silhouette are already a blend of object and ground — opaque in any matte, and a light outline over a dark room. Composited at draw scale over a dark ground, the rim's brightness lift falls from 0.836 of the interior's to 0.245 at 2px, for 2.1% of the object's area. Both were looked at, not only measured.

framing_rule.basis: Two acceptance numbers that decide which images ship, and which were literals inside matte.py — outside the freeze and outside `thresholds_sha256`, so the record's traceability claim did not cover them. max_border_off_fraction 0.02 checks the contract's own `framing.margin` ('full object centered, generous even margin on every side'): a 1-px border ring more than 2% of which is further than tolerance from the sampled ground means the object is touching the frame, the border median is contaminated, and the silhouette would come out bitten. 2% of a 3600-px ring is 72 px — a real intrusion, not a stray antialias pixel. The luminance band 40..215 checks the ground clause the tolerance rule cites as its whole authority; its first job is catching an already-matted PNG flattened onto black (median 0, whole frame reads as object, an opaque rectangle ships green), and 40/215 bound 'mid-grey' loosely enough that a legitimately dim or bright studio still passes.

cavity.scale_open_basis: `slide.scale_open` is the part's size multiplier at full travel — a drawer front approaching the viewer grows. The bounds were a bare `0.2 <= scale_open <= 3.0` inside a hard gate and outside the identity hash. They are sanity rails and not a fitted number: below 0.2 the part has vanished, above 3.0 it is larger than the carcass it came out of, and either is a mistyped flag rather than a judgement.
cavity.basis: min_carcass_backing 0.80 is the bound the corpus desk actually needed: a drawer slides out of a carcass and stays against it, and travel that carries the front past the carcass leaves it hanging over the leg gaps. Neither the clearance bound nor the canvas bound can see that -- the space between the legs is still on the canvas. overshoot_fraction 0.25 is the upper bound that keeps the open front AT its opening: a drawer slides out of its recess and stays at it, and with only a lower bound the corpus desk at dy 0.24 put the open front 79 body px below the recess -- eight pixels clear of it at the real 89 px draw height, straddling the stretchers, reading as a plank on the floor while twelve gates stayed green. max_dx_fraction 0.35 bounds sideways travel the same way. clearance_fraction 0.5 is where an anchored child's base lands in the recess: the open front's top edge must fall at or below it, or a revealed key draws on the face of the drawer instead of inside it (architecture.md's note on the placeholder desk's slide.dy 0.24). It is deliberately independent of `slide` -- an earlier draft derived the cavity FROM the slide, which made the clearance check compute its own threshold from the value it was checking and unable to fail for any input. 0.45 is src/placeholders.js's own recess factor, so an ingested body satisfies the same body/part luminance ratio (< 0.7) mechanisms.spec asserts for the placeholders. agreement_tolerance_fraction is how far a flagged drawer_cavity may sit from the derived one, as a fraction of the part's height, before it is a hard error naming both rectangles.

thumb.basis: §9.3c says 'content-bbox-centred crop, 128px'; a 128px crop of a 919px desk is a patch of oak, so this scales instead — a declared deviation. LANCZOS was chosen by looking: at the ~8x decimation a real sprite needs, nearest-neighbour drops the teardrop pulls and the reveal gaps and leaves a tile that reads as noise. Both are deterministic.

preview.basis: Blueprint §5's own arithmetic for the desk as it is actually staged: floor_against, so its baseline is yAtDepth(dims_m.d) and its scale is scaleAtDepth(0.55) = 96 * 3.5 / (3.5 - 0.55) = 113.9 px/m, giving 0.78m * 113.9 = 89px in the 1536px frame — NOT the 75px the bare wall scale of 96 px/m suggests. The sprite is therefore drawn at roughly a 10x downscale, which is the scale every edge decision here has to be judged at.

output.basis: A stored-resolution policy, pinned here because row 3 freezes it and rows 4 and 6 pay for it. The matte trims to content and does not upscale; a sprite whose content exceeds 384px is downsampled to it. Above that the sprite carries detail no draw scale can show: blueprint §5's own arithmetic puts the corpus desk on screen at 89 px, so 384 is already a 4.3x supersample — enough for the renderer's bilinear draw to have real information at every screen pixel, and enough headroom for a nearer staging depth. Stored at the arriving 914 px the same sprite aliased at 6.6x the placeholder's high-frequency energy in the drawn region; at 384 it measures 2.3x. Row 4's route is a bake embedding library PNGs as data: URIs in a document that must load from file:// with zero network requests, where every stored pixel is base64-inflated into the page, and this cap is what bounds it. NOTE, stated rather than buried: 384 is BELOW gate (c)'s 512 floor, and deliberately — gate (c) judges the resolution that ARRIVED (the matted source, per §9.4(c)'s 'content bbox', a statement about what the generator produced) and this policy governs what is STORED. Conflating them would either forbid storing near draw scale or hollow the gate out. An earlier version of this basis described a 1024 policy in full, beside the value 384: the anti-tuning scheme rests on a basis reading as the derivation of the number next to it, and that one derived a different number.

vocabularies.basis: One home for both vocabularies. `anchored` is the token row 2 minted for anchor-hosted takeables (blueprint §6, [AI] note); the shipped fixture validator requires anchor_on staging for exactly these. A test cross-checks the shipped src/placeholders.js records against this list without making that file the authority, since row 4 replaces it.
